statement: Encode/decode command word: 3-bit sync, RT addr(5), T/R(1), subaddr/mode(5), word count/mode code(5), 1 parity bit; word count 0 = 32 words
rationale: Basis of every message; wrong packing breaks C/Ada interop

statement: Encode/decode status word: sync, RT addr(5), ME/INSTR/SR/BCR/BUSY/SF/DBCA/TF bits, reserved=0, 1 parity bit
rationale: RT's only channel to report message/terminal condition

statement: Encode/decode data word: data sync (opposite polarity), 16-bit field, 1 parity bit
rationale: Sync polarity distinguishes data from command/status words

statement: Encode each word as 20 Manchester II bit cells (3 sync+16 data+1 parity) at 1 Mbit/s = 20us/word; decode reports Manchester violation on missing mid-bit transition
rationale: Detectable fault + real target for injector

statement: Generate odd parity on transmit; verify parity+sync on receive; flag invalid on failure
rationale: Basic word-level integrity check underlying CBIT

statement: Cyclic schedule: major frame of minor frames, message list/slot/period from config, detect+report minor frame overrun
rationale: Deterministic scheduling is the standard 1553 operating model
source: MIL-STD-1553B BC operation; frame structure derived

statement: Support BC-to-RT (receive, 1-32 data words, RT status) and RT-to-BC (transmit, RT status, 1-32 data words); check received count vs command count
rationale: The two fundamental message formats

statement: Support RT-to-RT: receive command then transmit command; validate both status words and command word-count consistency
rationale: Most error-prone format (two commands, two statuses, one data block)

statement: Issue mode commands with/without data word (subaddr 00000/11111) and broadcast commands (RT 31); no status expected on broadcast
rationale: False no-response would be declared if BC waited on broadcast

statement: Leave >=4us inter-message gap; declare no-response if no status begins within 14us of end of command word
rationale: Defines BC side of timing contract checked against RT response time

statement: RT acts only on own address or broadcast(31); validate parity/sync of every word, T/R bit, subaddr/mode, word count before executing
rationale: Executing unvalidated command is the RT's main hazard

statement: RT status word begins 4-12us after end of command word (valid command requiring response)
rationale: Outside window is a protocol violation (false timeout or gap collision)

statement: RT status bits: ME on rejected message; BUSY while subsystem busy; SF/TF from subsystem/BIT; RT addr always own address
rationale: BC makes recovery decisions from these bits

statement: RT-to-RT: receiving RT accepts data then responds with status after last word; transmitting RT responds to transmit command with status then data
rationale: Each RT sees only part of an RT-to-RT message

statement: RT handles supported mode codes (mode_code_table.md) with/without data word, including status-return, BIT-word, initiate-self-test codes
rationale: Mode codes manage the RT and trigger IBIT externally

statement: RT accepts/executes valid broadcast without status word; sets BCR in next status word; kept separate from fault-driven suppression
rationale: Simultaneous responses cause bus contention; correctly-silent must differ from faulty-silent

statement: Transmission error: discard, ME set, no response. Illegal command (valid transmission): no execute, ME set, status word sent. Busy: status with BUSY set, no data
rationale: Lets BC distinguish bus problem from command problem

statement: Record every word on bus A and B with timestamp/bus/validity flag; never transmit or influence bus traffic
rationale: Independent evidence source for timeline/response-time views

statement: Bus model with 2 independent channels A/B, modeled timing; BC/RT/BM communicate only via bus_transport_contract.md, no shared in-process state
rationale: Enables cross-language HSI evidence and mirrors separate-LRU partitioning

statement: On no-response or bus fault, BC retries once on alternate bus before declaring RT failed for the cycle; primary bus switch + degraded report on repeated consecutive failure
rationale: Redundancy is only useful with deterministic, visible failover
source: MIL-STD-1553B redundant bus provisions; policy derived

statement: PBIT at power-up: RAM walking 1/0, ROM checksum, encoder/decoder loopback, timer sanity, bus A/B idle check; failure blocks OPERATIONAL
rationale: RT that can't trust its own memory/codec must not answer commands

statement: CBIT during operation: parity on every word, protocol conformance, per-bus health counters, scheduler/service watchdog, no timing disturbance
rationale: How faults developing in service are found

statement: IBIT on request: full loopback both channels, cross-channel comparison, known-pattern echo verification, return to prior state after
rationale: Deeper on-ground/on-demand check than CBIT

statement: BIT results reported via TF/SF status bits, transmit-BIT-word mode command, internal result structure, health monitor API
rationale: Same result must be visible over the bus and locally

statement: Every terminal detects parity error, invalid sync, Manchester violation on each received word; reject message; update counters
rationale: First line of defense against corrupted traffic

statement: BC detects no-response, wrong RT address in status, unexpected ME/BUSY/SF/TF, word count mismatch; reacts per REDUN-001/BC-005
rationale: BC is the point where message-level faults become recovery actions

statement: Every detected error recorded in fixed-size non-overwriting-on-read log (timestamp, terminal, bus, type, msg id) with overflow counter; readable via health monitor API
rationale: Error records are the observed side of every injection comparison

statement: Release build contains no error injection code/data; release build inputs exclude errinject sources; release link map has no errinject symbols
rationale: Certification argument is absence from object code, not disabled flag

statement: Test-build error injection inert until harness arms via dedicated interface AND scenario file SHA-256 matches error_scenarios.sig; any failure leaves it inert and logged
rationale: Prevents accidental/unreviewed scenarios from perturbing a run

statement: Test-build injector supports PARITY_BIT_FLIP, CORRUPT_SYNC, SUPPRESS_RESPONSE, DELAY_RESPONSE, WRONG_WORD_COUNT, STATUS_BIT_INJECT(BUSY/ME/SF/TF), ILLEGAL_COMMAND, BUS_A_FAIL, BUS_B_FAIL; produces structured result record per scenario
rationale: Operational requirements of the injector as a DO-330 verification tool

statement: Pack/unpack command word fields (RT addr 0-31, T/R, subaddr/mode 0-31, word count/mode code 0-31) per layout; reject out-of-range field without producing a word
rationale: One bit layout defined once keeps C/Ada byte-identical on the bus

statement: Map data count 1-32 to word count field 1-31/0 (32=0) and back; reject encode request for 0 or >32
rationale: 32-as-zero is the classic off-by-one defect

statement: Pack/unpack status word fields (RT addr, ME/INSTR/SR/BCR/BUSY/SF/DBCA/TF), reserved bits=0 on pack; unpack flags non-zero reserved bits
rationale: Reserved-nonzero is a detectable anomaly, not something to mask

statement: Pack/unpack data word (16-bit value, data sync) with bit-exact transparency
rationale: Data words carry no structure at word level

statement: Compute odd parity over 16-bit info field; provide check function returning valid/invalid
rationale: Single source of parity for encoder/decoder/BIT/monitor

statement: Encode word as 40 half-bit symbols: cmd/status sync=1,1,1,0,0,0; data sync=0,0,0,1,1,1; each bit as 1,0 (one) or 0,1 (zero), MSB first
rationale: Fixes exact on-bus symbol sequence, the injector's corruption target

statement: Decode 40 symbols to sync type/field/parity; classify sync by exact pattern match; report Manchester violation on any 0,0 or 1,1 data/parity cell
rationale: Detection point for WORD-004 and ERR-001

statement: Classify every received word as exactly one of VALID/SYNC_ERROR/MANCHESTER_ERROR/PARITY_ERROR in that precedence order; decoded fields only when VALID
rationale: Single ordered classification prevents drift between terminals

statement: Schedule table: fixed-capacity entries (type, RT addr(es), subaddr, word count, mode code, minor frame index, slot offset, preferred bus); validated at init, rejected if invalid (scheduler stays IDLE)
rationale: Static, validated schedule; no dynamic allocation

statement: Start messages at slot offset within minor frame; advance minor frame after configured period; wrap major frame; raise MINOR_FRAME_OVERRUN if last message incomplete by period end
rationale: Deterministic cycle plus explicit overrun detection

statement: BC-to-RT: transmit receive command, N data words back to back, wait for one status word; complete on valid status
rationale: Defines exact word order for receive format

statement: RT-to-BC: transmit transmit command, wait for status then N data words; complete only if status valid and exactly N valid data words received
rationale: Word count check on receive side catches short/long response

statement: RT-to-RT: transmit receive command immediately followed by transmit command; expect xmit-RT status, N data, recv-RT status; reject mismatched word counts; complete only if both statuses valid and addresses match
rationale: Two commands, two statuses, one data block must all be accounted for

statement: Issue mode command with mode indicator subaddr (00000/11111) and listed mode code; transmit/receive the one data word per mode_code_table.md when defined; reject unlisted mode code
rationale: Ties BC behavior to the same table the RT uses

statement: Broadcast: transmit command + data words, no status wait; complete after last word plus gap
rationale: Waiting for status after broadcast would produce false no-response

statement: Start next message's command word no earlier than T_GAP_MIN_US after previous message end, or after no-response timeout expiry if applicable, whichever is later
rationale: Prevents BC violating its own timing rule after a timeout

statement: Start timer at end of last command word expecting response; declare NO_RESPONSE if no status start observed within T_NORESP_US; not earlier
rationale: Both directions matter: late wastes bandwidth, early falsely fails RTs

statement: BC state machine: IDLE/MAJOR_FRAME/MINOR_FRAME/WAIT_RESPONSE/TIMEOUT/FAILOVER/DEGRADED with fixed transition set (see SDD 5.1); other events ignored and counted
rationale: Explicit transitions is what the state machine viewer overlays coverage on

statement: Process command only if RT address matches own (0-30) or broadcast(31); silently ignore all others
rationale: An RT answering another RT's command creates bus contention

statement: Validate command against subaddress table (direction, word count range, subaddr/mode enabled) before execution; report VALID/ILLEGAL_SUBADDRESS/ILLEGAL_DIRECTION/ILLEGAL_WORD_COUNT
rationale: Separates the three illegal-command causes so each is testable

statement: Accept exactly N data words into subaddress buffer; commit only if all N valid; fewer/more before next command word is a word count error
rationale: Prevents a partially received block reaching the subsystem

statement: Transmit status word then exactly N data words from subaddress buffer, no gap between words
rationale: Word order and count for the transmit format

statement: Response timing state machine (WAIT_END_OF_WORD/DELAY_RUNNING/TRANSMIT_STATUS) with configured delay, default 8us; reject config value outside [4,12]us at init
rationale: Guarantees the 4-12us window by construction and config check

statement: Build status word: own RT address; ME set on rejection/cleared on next valid command; BUSY only while subsystem busy; SF/TF from subsystem/BIT; BCR set after broadcast, cleared on next non-broadcast valid command
rationale: Each bit gets an explicit set/clear condition, testable individually

statement: As xmit RT: answer transmit command after receive command to other RT with status+N data. As recv RT: wait for xmit RT status+N data, send own status only if all valid and count matches; else ME set, no status
rationale: Each RT sees only part of an RT-to-RT message

statement: Mode command dispatch via constant table (mode code, data presence/direction, handler); include transmit-status/initiate-self-test/transmit-BIT-word/reset/synchronize(w & w/o data); other codes = ILLEGAL
rationale: Table-driven dispatch keeps supported subset and BC table aligned

statement: Valid broadcast: same validation/execution as addressed command, no transmission, BCR set per RT-006, separate code path from fault-driven suppression
rationale: Correctly-silent and faulty-silent must be distinguishable in code and tests

statement: On any word classified other than VALID, or word count error: discard message, ME set, transmit nothing, record error per ERR-004
rationale: A message with a transmission error must not be executed nor answered

statement: Command VALID at word level but fails RT-002 validation or names unsupported mode code: no execute, ME set, status word (no data) sent after configured delay
rationale: BC needs an answer to distinguish illegal command from bus fault

statement: Subsystem busy: no execute, status with BUSY set and no data words; no data transmitted on transmit command
rationale: Busy means cannot serve, must not answer with stale data

statement: RT state machine: RESET/IDLE/WAIT_COMMAND/VALIDATE/EXECUTE/RESPOND/ERROR/BUSY/FAIL_SAFE with fixed transitions (see SDD 5.2); FAIL_SAFE answers with TF set, no data
rationale: Explicit transitions for coverage overlay; FAIL_SAFE keeps RT visible to BC

statement: Capture every word on channels A/B into fixed-capacity record buffer (bus, start time, 40 symbols, classification); count dropped records on overflow
rationale: Source buffer for timeline and response-time views

statement: Group captured words into messages by command word and inter-message gap; classify message type; compute response time from end of command to start of status
rationale: Response time and message type are required outputs for visualizations

statement: BM accesses bus model only through receive interface; no transmit function reachable from bm_monitor (no call, no reference)
rationale: Proves by construction that the monitor cannot influence traffic

statement: Two independent channels A/B; word on one channel delivered unchanged to all connected terminals/monitor on that channel only; failed channel delivers nothing
rationale: Channel independence is what makes A/B failover testable

statement: Exchange words per bus_transport_contract.md (type, channel, start time, 40 symbols, terminal id, version field), fixed byte layout; reject unknown version or malformed layout
rationale: Contract, not shared code, ties the two implementations together

statement: Deterministic virtual clock in microseconds, advanced only by word durations and explicit waits; all timestamps from this clock; never read host clock for protocol timing
rationale: Timing results must be reproducible on any workstation

statement: On NO_RESPONSE or word-level error, retransmit same message exactly once on alternate bus after inter-message gap; use retry result as message result
rationale: One deterministic retry

statement: Count consecutive failed messages per bus; at threshold (default 3) on primary, designate other bus primary, reset counters, record failover event, enter DEGRADED
rationale: Distinguishes an RT problem from a bus problem

statement: When retry also fails, mark RT failed for current major frame, skip its remaining messages, clear mark at next major frame start; expose failed-RT flags and DEGRADED via health monitor API
rationale: Avoids wasting the schedule on a dead RT while still retrying later

statement: Walking-ones/zeros pattern test over each RAM region under test, restore contents afterward, report address of first mismatch
rationale: Detects stuck bits in buffers used for data words

statement: Compute checksum over configured code/constant region, compare with stored reference, report failure on mismatch
rationale: Detects corrupted constants such as the mode code table

statement: Encode known words, decode symbols and compare for command/status/data words; verify timer advances by expected amount within 1us tolerance
rationale: Exercises encode/decode paths and the time source

statement: Verify no word activity on channels A/B for defined listen period; combine all PBIT results; prevent OPERATIONAL entry if any PBIT test failed
rationale: Implements the blocking behavior of HLR-BIT-001

statement: For each received word/message evaluate WORD-008 classification, word count consistency, and response time against 4-12us window; increment matching violation counter
rationale: Continuous version of the same checks, using the same functions

statement: Keep good-message/error counters per channel; declare channel unhealthy when error ratio over window exceeds threshold; watchdog reports fault if BC/RT loop misses its progress period
rationale: Provides bus health data for redundancy decisions and hang detection

statement: On request, transmit known pattern on each channel, verify echo, compare channels, report difference, restore prior state; no effect on messages to other terminals
rationale: The deeper test required by HLR-BIT-003

statement: Maintain result structure per level (test id, pass/fail, failing item, timestamp); set TF on fatal/SF on non-fatal; provide BIT word for transmit-BIT-word mode code; read-only health monitor API access
rationale: One result, three views (bus, BIT word, local API)

statement: BIT state machine: POWER_UP/PBIT/OPERATIONAL/CBIT_RUNNING/IBIT_RUNNING/DEGRADED/FAIL with fixed transitions (see SDD 5.3)
rationale: Explicit transitions for the state machine viewer

statement: On any word classified other than VALID: reject enclosing message, increment counter for error type+channel, create error record per ERR-004
rationale: Common reaction, shared by BC, RT and BM

statement: Check every received status word for RT address match and ME/BUSY/SF/TF bits; report specific mismatch type each with its scheduled reaction (retry for ME/address mismatch, report-only for BUSY/SF/TF)
rationale: BC-side decision table for status bits

statement: Detect mismatch between command word count and valid data words received (fewer or more); report WORD_COUNT_MISMATCH; treat message as failed
rationale: Covers the wrong-word-count fault class end to end

statement: Fixed-capacity error log (default 64 records): timestamp, terminal, channel, error type, message id; discard-newest on overflow with overflow counter; read-only via health monitor API
rationale: First fault is usually the one that matters; discard-newest keeps it

statement: Release build definitions exclude all errinject files; no release source references an errinject symbol; build step fails if release link map contains an errinject symbol
rationale: Certification argument is absence from certified object code

statement: Test-build injector inert until armed via harness-token interface; returns to inert on disarm/process start; rejects arm without token, logs rejection
rationale: Runtime gate (a) of HLR-ERR-005

statement: Before arming, compute SHA-256 of error_scenarios.yaml, compare to error_scenarios.sig; stay inert and log rejection if mismatched or signature absent
rationale: Runtime gate (b) of HLR-ERR-005; every executed scenario was reviewed and signed

statement: Implement each fault primitive at the bus_model.bus_transmit interposition point: PARITY_BIT_FLIP, CORRUPT_SYNC, SUPPRESS_RESPONSE, DELAY_RESPONSE, WRONG_WORD_COUNT, STATUS_BIT_INJECT(BUSY/ME/SF/TF), ILLEGAL_COMMAND, BUS_A_FAIL, BUS_B_FAIL, per scenario target/channel/word index/count
rationale: Each primitive changes only what its name says, so detection is attributable

statement: Execute each signed scenario in order; compare observed detection/recovery (error log, BIT results, bus record) to expected; emit result record (scenario_id, timestamp_us, terminal, bus, fault, expected, observed, pass_fail, HLR, LLR, test_id); no-detection scenario recorded as failure
rationale: A missed detection must never default to pass
